content.summary: In this reading, you will follow a short workplace report about sales, customer numbers, and market share. You will practise finding the main message, locating figures, and understanding how prepositions such as from, to, by, and at describe changes in data.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Use verbs of change with adverbs, such as increased steadily, and noun phrases such as a slight decline. Use from and to for starting and ending values, by for the amount of change, and at for a specific level.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Words and phrases for business trends, including increase steadily, drop sharply, remain stable, peak at, fluctuate, and a slight decline.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Skim the report first to understand its main message. Then scan for years, percentages, and other figures. Check the words before and after each number to understand what it describes.

learningObjectives: Understand the main idea of a short report about changes in workplace data.
Locate specific details such as years, percentages, and sales figures.
Recognize trend verbs, trend nouns, and adverbs that describe the speed or size of a change.
Identify how from, to, by, and at are used with numbers.

contextWarmup.prompt: A company reports that its online sales went from 20,000 units to 28,000 units in one year. Which sentence describes the change correctly?
options: Online sales increased from 20,000 to 28,000 units.
Online sales increased at 20,000 to 28,000 units.
Online sales increased by 20,000 to 28,000 units.
contextWarmup.explanation: Use from for the starting figure and to for the ending figure. By is used for the amount of change, not for the two values in this sentence.

rules: Use a verb of change with an adverb to describe how a figure changes: Sales increased steadily.
Use There was followed by an adjective and a noun of change for a more formal report style: There was a slight decline in sales.
Use from and to for the start and end values, by for the amount of change, and at for a level: The rate rose from 4% to 6%, a rise of 2 percentage points, and then remained stable at 6%.

commonTrap.explanation: Learners sometimes use by when they mean the ending value. By describes the size of a change, while to gives the new level.
commonTrap.correct: The price rose from $10 to $15. It increased by $5.

content.passageTitle: A Year of Change at Northstar Foods
paragraphs: Northstar Foods reviewed its online sales at the end of 2024. Sales increased steadily from 20,000 orders in January to 28,000 in May. They peaked at 32,000 orders in July, after a summer advertising campaign. The company says that faster delivery and a new website helped attract more customers.

After July, orders dropped sharply to 24,000 in September, then recovered to 27,000 in November. The number of store customers remained stable at around 18,000 each month. Northstar's market share rose from 12% to 15% over the year, an increase of 3 percentage points. Managers plan to study the autumn fall before setting next year's targets.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Reporting Workplace Trends and Data

content.summary: Learn how to describe workplace trends and numerical data clearly using dynamic verbs, noun phrases, and correct numerical prepositions in business reports.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Verb and Adverb Formula
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + Verb of Change + Adverb + Time Expression
blueprintItems.example: Online sales increased steadily throughout the first quarter of 2024.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Formal Noun Phrase Formula
blueprintItems.formula: There was / were + a/an + Adjective + Noun of Change + in + Subject
blueprintItems.example: There was a dramatic fall in customer complaints after the new policy was introduced.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Numerical Data Prepositions
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + Verb + from [Start Number] + to [End Number] / by [Difference] / at [Point]
blueprintItems.example: The number of employees rose from 150 to 320 between 2019 and 2023, increasing by 170 staff members.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use 'by' to show the amount of change, 'from... to' for the start and end points, and 'at' to state a specific level.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Profits rose to 10% when they started at 50,000 dollars and finished at 55,000 dollars.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Profits rose by 10%, increasing from 50,000 dollars to 55,000 dollars.
mechanicsRules.why: 'To' shows the final number, while 'by' marks the specific difference between the two numbers.

mechanicsRules.rule: Avoid mixing adjectives with verbs of change; pair adjectives with nouns and adverbs with verbs.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Website traffic grew dramatic last month.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Website traffic grew dramatically last month, or there was a dramatic growth in traffic.
mechanicsRules.why: Adverbs modify verbs like 'grew', whereas adjectives modify nouns like 'growth'.

mechanicsRules.rule: Always capitalize formal quarter abbreviations and specific months when reporting timelines.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Sales dropped sharply in q3 and november.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Sales dropped sharply in Q3 and November.
mechanicsRules.why: Business quarters such as Q1 or Q3 and months of the year are proper nouns and formal acronyms.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Workplace Trends and Data

content.summary: Practise describing simple workplace charts with clear trend verbs and accurate number prepositions. Use increase steadily for a gradual rise, drop sharply for a fast fall, remain stable for little or no change, and fluctuate for repeated rises and falls.
content.audioGuidance: Say the trend phrase clearly, then pause briefly before the figure or time period. Use at before a specific value after peak or remain stable, and between before the two ends of a range. Stress the main words, such as increased, sharply, and sales.

pillars.name: Vowel Clarity
pillars.target: Clear vowel sounds in key trend words
pillars.explanation: Say the long vowel in peak clearly, and keep the vowel in drop short. Clear vowels help listeners distinguish important chart terms.

pillars.name: Word Stress
pillars.target: Stress the important part of trend words
pillars.explanation: Give the main stress to the second syllable in increase and decline. In fluctuate, stress the first syllable.

pillars.name: Number Prepositions
pillars.explanation: Say sales peaked at 80,000. For a range, say the figure fluctuated between 60,000 and 75,000.

pillars.name: Presentation Rhythm
pillars.target: Group trend, figure, and time period
pillars.explanation: Keep related information together, as in Sales increased steadily to 80,000 last year. Pause between separate points on the chart.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: Keep the main stress on crease when you add the ending.
The main stress stays on the second syllable in declining.
The stress moves from the first syllable in fluctuate to the third syllable in fluctuation.
The stress moves from the first syllable in stable to the second syllable in stability.

reading.question: What is the report mainly about?

reading.explanation: 'Economic' refers to national financial systems, while 'economical' refers to frugality or efficiency.

reading.question: Select the sentence expressing an unfulfilled past obligation using modal perfects:
